svg.text: PART A - PC register (reset mux, stall-hold mux, FF) -> inst_fetch_pc_o
PART B - instruction path: two NOP-insert muxes (as in the sketch)
PART C - branch flush shift register (squash the two instructions fetched behind a taken branch)
Fig P1 - Pipeline Stage 1 (IF): PC register, instruction NOP muxes, branch-flush shift register
Drawn from the team's IF/ID sketches. Where a sketch was ambiguous the choice is noted in italics - check it against your RTL.
fetch_pc_i[31:0] (next PC from EX, Fig P5)
reset = 1 -> PC = 0. stall_read_i = 1 (data-memory read in flight) -> PC holds. Otherwise PC <= fetch_pc_i = (branch ? target : PC + 4) computed in EX.
Muxes as in the sketch: input 0 = NOP, input 1 = instruction; select 1 = inst_mem_is_valid, then stall_read_i.
NOP = addi x0,x0,0 (32'h00000013). The polarity of the second select (stall_read_i) is read from the sketch - verify it against your RTL.
A taken branch is only known in EX, two instructions later.
wb_stall_first_o = 1 for the instruction right behind it,
wb_stall_second_o = 1 for the one after that.
Both are used in WB to suppress their register write and
memory write (Fig P9) - same trick as the 2-FF chain in your
Hold-mux select, as drawn in the sketch:
upd_en = ~stall_read_i & (wb_mem_to_reg_i & d_mem_write_valid_i) -> select = 1 loads the new value, 0 holds.
The AND-gate inputs are read from the sketch - verify them against your RTL.
